note: The DECLARED, BOUNDED set the diff-scoped mutation gate may report NOT_APPLICABLE for instead of UNKNOWN, because the cost of measuring it has been measured and is not the diff's. Owner rulings 2026-10-03 (`capture.py`) and 2026-10-11 (`webmon.py`): TWO module-level declarations, named. A bare `module.py` key declares the whole module and needs `cost.scope: module` with both module measurements; a `module.py::function` key needs `cost.scope: function`. The permitted module keys are an owner-named ALLOWLIST, not a count (`mutation_diff.MODULE_KEYS_AUTHORIZED`): a module key for anything the rulings do not name refuses, even as the only entry — a bound of two would say "two modules are declarable" and hand the second slot to any module, which is the general permission neither ruling gave. Read mutation_diff.parse_exclusions for the shapes it refuses, declared_module for what matches, and declared_exclusion_status for the only transition allowed (UNKNOWN or NOT_RUN -> NOT_APPLICABLE; never a survivor cleared, never a PASS). The gate consults this at SELECTION, before the clean run, so a declared module costs seconds instead of the 7693 s #3238 spent reaching the same answer.
retiredWhen: mutmut applies the glob at GENERATION as well as at RUN, so a one-function diff stops paying for the module's whole population. capture.py then becomes measurable function by function and this file goes to empty — the exclusion is dated debt, not a design.

capture.py.reason: THIS IS A MODULE-LEVEL FACT, not a claim about any one function: `mutmut run <glob>` applies the glob when it RUNS mutants and never when it GENERATES them, so every capture.py diff pays for the whole module's population whatever it touched. No function of capture.py is measurable inside the 7200 s gate budget on the runner, and no narrowing of a diff reaches that cost. Measured twice, by two independent mechanisms: by TIME, #3238 presented the ideal case — one 87-line function and one keyword argument — and still reached no mutant, with selection plus clean run 1337 s, generation under 1 s, then a silent traced stats pass of at least 7556 s; 618 spinner lines carried ZERO `N/M` ticks, which is what proves nothing was tested rather than merely slow. By MEMORY, one `mutmut run` worker reached 8.2 GB RSS importing the 536 MB generated module — above the fleet's 8 GB standing per-process limit, while mutmut spawns one worker per core — and was killed by hand after 21 minutes with `--timeout 900` never firing. Superseded E7's two function keys (`capture.py::_cpap_stream_watch_row`, `capture.py::_maybe_start_cpap_spool_pull`), which could never fire once this key exists; their measurements are the evidence cited here.

webmon.py.reason: THIS IS A MODULE-LEVEL FACT about where the cost sits, not a claim about any one handler: `make_app` is a single 1,791-line factory (webmon.py:187-1977) holding 57 nested handler closures, so every handler edit scopes the whole factory, and `mutmut` applies a glob when it RUNS mutants and never when it GENERATES them. Mutant GENERATION therefore does not finish inside the gate's own generation cap, and no narrowing of a diff reaches that cost: a 76-line diff across 5 functions still pays for the module's whole population. Measured three times, twice in CI and once locally, and the two mechanisms agree on the phase — generation, not the stats pass that bounds capture.py. The local run is the one that names the phase explicitly: the gate killed generation AT its 3496 s cap with 450 MiB of mutants written and NO mutant run. Retire this entry by splitting make_app into module-level handlers (WEBMON-MAKE-APP-SPLIT), after which a handler diff scopes a handler and the module is measurable function by function.
webmon.py.retiredBy: WEBMON-MAKE-APP-SPLIT — split `make_app` into module-level handlers so a handler edit scopes one function. The brief is to be created by the session that takes the split; this entry is dated debt, not a design.

cost.generationCapNote: 3496 s is the CAP, not an elapsed measurement: it is GENERATION_CAP_FRACTION (0.5) x the 6992 s of gate budget left when webmon started. Generation was killed BY that deadline, with elapsed printed as 3496 s at :.0f precision, so it overran by under a second and the true requirement is only bounded below: generation needs MORE than 3496 s on rig-x870. The tool reports when the cap fires, never by how much a run would have overshot it.
cost.generatedBytesNote: A LOWER BOUND, and reconstructed from a rounded display: the log prints 450 MiB at :.0f over st_size/1024**2, so the exact byte count is 450 MiB +/- 0.5 MiB and 471859200 is its midpoint. The scratch directory was removed and the --json was never written (emit runs at the end and the run was ended first), so the exact figure is not recoverable. It is a lower bound on the complete module because generation was killed PARTWAY: a finished generation writes more.
cost.mutantsGeneratedNote: NOT RECORDED, and deliberately absent rather than 0 (§∅): generation never completed and mutmut prints no count until it does, so how many mutants existed at the kill is unknown. `mutantsDecided` IS 0, which is a measurement — no mutant ran.
cost.memoryNote: NO memory figure is cited because none was measured: no VmHWM, no `time -v`, no cgroup peak was taken on any process in these runs. An intermediate relay of the local result described the 450 MiB as memory; the session that ran it corrected that to bytes on disk. capture.py's entry carries a `workerRssBytes` because that run was instrumented for it; this one was not, and an uninstrumented run yields no number rather than a plausible one.
cost.moduleFunctionsNote: 64 counts nested functions, which is the point here: 7 are module-level and 57 are closures inside `make_app` (measured by AST over webmon.py at origin/main, 2026-10-11). `count_module_functions` reports the same 64. The factory's span is 187-1977, 1,791 lines.
